<Norway> competed at the [2022 Winter Olympics](2022_Winter_Olympics "2022 Winter Olympics") in <Beijing>, China, from 4 to 20 February 2022.[[1]](Norway_at_the_2022_Winter_Olympics#cite_note-1)[[2]](Norway_at_the_2022_Winter_Olympics#cite_note-2) The Norwegian team consisted of 84 athletes.[[3]](Norway_at_the_2022_Winter_Olympics#cite_note-noc-entries-norway-3) [Kjetil Jansrud](Kjetil_Jansrud "Kjetil Jansrud") and [Kristin Skaslien](Kristin_Skaslien "Kristin Skaslien") were the country's flagbearers during the [opening ceremony](2022_Winter_Olympics_opening_ceremony "2022 Winter Olympics opening ceremony").[[4]](Norway_at_the_2022_Winter_Olympics#cite_note-fl-4) Biathlete [Marte Olsbu Røiseland](Marte_Olsbu_R%C3%B8iseland "Marte Olsbu Røiseland") was the flag bearer during the [closing ceremony](2022_Winter_Olympics_closing_ceremony "2022 Winter Olympics closing ceremony").[[5]](Norway_at_the_2022_Winter_Olympics#cite_note-5)

Three days before the closing ceremony, Norway won its 14th gold medal, thus matching its record performance of [2018](Norway_at_the_2018_Winter_Olympics "Norway at the 2018 Winter Olympics"), as well as Canada's [2010](Canada_at_the_2010_Winter_Olympics "Canada at the 2010 Winter Olympics") and Germany's [2018](Germany_at_the_2018_Winter_Olympics "Germany at the 2018 Winter Olympics") results. Norway won its 15th gold medal on 18 February, thus breaking the record.
This should be seen in light of the ongoing medal inflation, e.g., from 16 gold medals in [1924](1924_Winter_Olympics_medal_table "1924 Winter Olympics medal table") to 109 in 2022. However, Norway also holds the medal inflation-adjusted records: in [1936](1936_Winter_Olympics_medal_table "1936 Winter Olympics medal table"), Norwegian athletes won 41% of all events (7 out of 17), in [1928](1928_Winter_Olympics_medal_table "1928 Winter Olympics medal table"), 43% (6 out of 14). As of 20 February 2022, this percentage for the 2022 Games stands at ~14%.
